NUYDA, CESO Ill Regional Director Cordillera Administrative Region Baguio City Dear Regional Director Nuyda: This refers to the Memorandum dated April 2, 2025, from then DILG CAR Regional Director Araceli A. San Jose requesting the Department's legal opinion on whether the City of Baguio may still implement an ordinance granting financial assistance to Local Government Units (LGUs) that were placed under a state of calamity in 2024. per the representation, the City Government of Baguio enacted an ordinance. The 2024 Quick Response Fund (QRF) under the City Disaster Risk, Reduction and Management Fund (CDRRMF), allotted One Million Pesos (Php as financial assistance to Batanes, while the Five Hundred Thousand Pesos (Php 500,000.00) was appropriated for Negros Occidental. Unfortunately, these amounts were never released due to failure to process purchase request prior to the closure of the accounting books for year 2024. In light of these, Mayor Magalong posed the following questions — I. Can the City Government of Baguio proceed with the donation without amending the ordinance and charge the amount to the Trust Fund, considering that the financial assistance was previously approved under the 2024 appropriation? Or Should the City Government request for a supplemental AIP to include the donations for both provinces? 2. Can the City Government of Baguio proceed with the donation using the Trust Fund even though the state of calamity in the recipient provinces was declared in 2024? Would this be consistent with the provisions of the Local Government Code and other relevant laws and guidelines governing the use of LDRRMF and Trust Funds? Since both questions are interrelated, we shall jointly discuss the same. At the onset, we concur with the assertion initially submitted by RD San Jose that the City of Baguio is no longer in a position to proceed with the intended donation, given that there is no longer a state of calamity. And that is regardless of submission of an Annual Investment Plan. Section 21 of Republic Act No. 10121 otherwise known as the Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010, specially provides, that — "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

"Section 21. Local Disaster Risk" Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF). - The present Local Calamity Fund shall henceforth be known as the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF). Not less than five percent (5%) of the estimated revenue from regular sources shall be set aside as the LDRRMF to support disaster risk management activities such as, but not limited to, pre- disaster preparedness programs including training, purchasing life- saving rescue equipment, supplies and medicines, for post-disaster activities, and for the payment of premiums on calamity insurance. The LDRRMC shall monitor and evaluate the use and disbursement of the LDRRMF based on the. LDRRMP as incorporated in the local development plans and annual work and financial plan. Upon the recommendation of the LDRRMO and approval of the sanggunian concerned, the LDRRMC may transfer the said fund to support disaster risk reduction work of other LDRRMCs which are declared under state of calamity. Of the amount appropriated for LDRRMF, thirty percent (30%) shall be allocated as Quick Response Fund (QRF) or stand-by fund for relief and recovery programs in order that situation and living conditions of people In communities or areas stricken by disasters, calamities, epidemics, or complex emergencies, may be normalized as quickly as possible. Unexpended LDRRMF shall accrue to a special trust fund solely for the purpose of supporting disaster risk reduction and management activities of the LDRRMCs within the next five (5) years. Any such amount still not fully utilized after five (5) years shall revert back to the general fund and will be available for other social services to be identified by the local sanggunian. xxx xxx xxx Further, under sections I, 2 and 3 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 10121„ provides for certain qualifications for the utilization of LDRRMF, thus - "Section 1. Utilization of the LDRRMF — The present Local Calamity Fund shall henceforth be known as the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF). The LDRRMC shall monitor and evaluate the use and disbursement of the LDRRMF based on the LDRRMP as incorporated in the local development plans and annual work and financial plan. Any such amount still not fully utilized after 5 yeans shall revert back to tho general fund and made available for other social setvices to be identified by the local Sanggunian. " Relatedly, in the NDRRMC-DBM-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2013-1 dated March 25, 2013 on the Allocation and Utilization of the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) states — 6.0 Policies and Procedures on the Utilization of the LDRRMF The following procedures shall be observed in the use of the LDRRMF subject to budgetind, accounting and auditing rules and regulations: xxx xxx xxx xxx xxx xxx xxx xxx xxx 6.4 The unexpended LDRRMF shall accrue to a special trust fund solely for the purpose of supporting disaster risk reduction and management activities of the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (LDRRMC) within the next five (5) years. xxx xxx xxx In Commission on Audit (COA) Circular No. 2012-002 dated September 12, 2012 particularly Item 5.1.10 specifically declares that — "5. I. IO All unexpended /unobligated balance of the QRF and the DRRMF- MOOE shall be transferred to the Special Trust Fund under the account "Trust Liability-DRRM in the Trust Fund Books. " Given the foregoing, the City Government of Baguio can no longer proceed with the intended donation since state of calamity has already ceased to exist. To recall, the use of QRF as provided for by law, is intended to address immediate needs of communities or areas stricken by disasters, calamities, epidemics, or complex emergencies. In the event that said fund is unexpended, then it will accrue to the trust fund and shall form part in the entirety of the LDRRMF that may be utilized for future LDRRMC activities. Page 3 of4

Finally, even if the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Baguio were to enact a supplemental appropriations accordance with the AIP, such transfer would remain inapplicable. This is due to the explicit provision of the law, which allows such fund transfers only when the recipient LGU has been declared under a state of calamity. In the absence of such declaration, there is no longer a valid legal basis for the release or transfer of the fund. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLA.'RPB,'LLLS-LLRALD/mag copy firnished: ARACELI A.
